findings.body: The vertical pseudo-element inset makes each collapsed disclosure’s hit area extend into adjacent table rows. The prior Emil ruling counted this as a 44px touch area, but it did not weigh the existing metrics in `frontend/app/globals.css:1498,1737,1742`: 11px text at 1.5 line-height plus 7px vertical cell padding produces a roughly 30.5px row, while `after:-inset-y-4` adds 32px to the button box. Consecutive targets therefore overlap by roughly 18px, so browser hit-testing can toggle the wrong row when a user taps the row padding. Give rows enough height for non-overlapping targets or constrain the expanded hit box to its row.
findings.title: Not done: keep disclosure touch targets within their rows

findings.body: The UI proof still supplies completed `rowLabels` through a mocked Ask API, while this task intentionally has no production caller for `GlNameRepository`. Consequently there is still no running-API, real-database browser test proving that resolved GL and statement labels reach the table and disclosure. The story assigns that production crossing to GL-ANSWER-WIRING, so this remains deferred advice rather than a blocker for this task alone.
